title: Anthropic IPO 6x Oversubscribed at $1.4T Valuation, Trading Nov 19
summary: Anthropic IPO 6x oversubscribed at $1.4T, trading Nov 19 on Nasdaq. Plus Claude for Manufacturing, the Nvidia overhang, and what builders should watch.

Anthropic IPO


# Anthropic IPO 6x Oversubscribed at $1.4T Valuation, Trading Nov 19


By OpenTools Team


·


November 13, 2026


Anthropic's IPO is six times oversubscribed at a $1.4 trillion valuation, with pricing set at $70–$78 per share for an 825 million share offering ahead of a November 19 Nasdaq debut under ticker ANT. The company simultaneously launched Claude for Manufacturing — a 17‑skill plugin for factory‑floor workers — and Claude Meetings, but a shadow hangs over Nvidia's $10 billion private‑placement pledge following Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO. For builders, this is the most consequential AI IPO since SpaceX: it will set the pricing benchmark for AI companies and determine how much capital flows into Claude's developer ecosystem.


## The IPO by the Numbers: $70–$78, 825M Shares, Nasdaq ANT


[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) is offering 825 million Class A shares at $70 to $78 each, the company disclosed in a[draft prospectus seen by Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/anthropic-ipo-raise-much-644-billion-latest-draft-prospectus-shows-2026-11-10/) . At the top of that range, the public offering would raise up to $64.4 billion, with an additional $26 billion in a concurrent private placement from seven cornerstone investors — Alphabet's[Google](https://opentools.ai/organizations/google) , Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron Technology,[Microsoft](https://opentools.ai/organizations/microsoft) , and TSMC — bringing the total raise to as much as $90.4 billion, larger than SpaceX's $85.7 billion IPO in June.


On a fully diluted basis, which includes stock options and restricted stock units, the valuation reaches approximately $1.4 trillion — up from the $965 billion private valuation from May but well below the $2 trillion figure floated in investor discussions as recently as October,[CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/10/anthropic-sets-price-range-of-70-to-78-in-upcoming-ipo.html) . Non-diluted market value is roughly $1 trillion. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the offering alongside more than 20 other banks. Pricing is set for November 18, with trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT beginning November 19.


## Six Times Oversubscribed — and the Valuation Strategy Behind It


The roadshow drew roughly six times more demand than available shares, driven by large anchor-style institutional orders,[Bloomberg reported](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-12/anthropic-s-ipo-is-said-to-be-about-six-times-oversubscribed) . The oversubscription validates the pricing strategy: by setting the range at $70–$78 — a roughly 20% discount to what many investors had been expecting —[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) is giving the market room to bid the stock up on debut rather than forcing a take-it-or-leave-it valuation.


"By seeking a valuation close to 20% below market expectations, this allows investors to 'bid up' the IPO rather than facing a take-it-or-leave-it scenario like SpaceX took," Jeff Zell of IPO Boutique told[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/anthropic-ipo-raise-much-644-billion-latest-draft-prospectus-shows-2026-11-10/) . It is a calculated bet: price conservatively, let demand drive the pop, and let the narrative be about momentum rather than overreach. One shareholder told CNBC that even a $1.5 trillion valuation was now "a stretch."


## Claude for Manufacturing: 17 Skills, 4 Connectors, and a Factory-Floor Bet


Two days into its IPO roadshow,[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) launched[Claude for Manufacturing](https://claude.com/resources/articles/claude-for-manufacturing) — a plugin with 17 pre-configured skills covering quoting, quality investigations, maintenance diagnosis, purchasing, design, and production reporting,[Business Insider reported](https://www.businessinsider.com/anthropic-launches-claude-for-manufacturers-ahead-of-ipo-2026-11) . The plugin connects to four enterprise systems: Autodesk Fusion for design data, Infor for procurement and stock lookups,[Microsoft](https://opentools.ai/organizations/microsoft) 365 for procedures and supplier emails, and Oracle NetSuite for production and financial records.


Anthropic's enterprise go-to-market lead Lauren Collett framed manufacturing as a signal of ambition: "Manufacturing is complex and judgment-heavy work. And I think that as model capabilities have advanced, this is just a really, really great time for us to be looking at some of these more complex business processes," she told[Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/anthropic-launches-claude-for-manufacturers-ahead-of-ipo-2026-11) . The plugin does not directly operate equipment — that capability is being researched separately — but it automates the paperwork, investigation, and reporting that surrounds factory-floor decisions, effectively letting experienced workers spend more time on judgment and less on back-office toil.


## The Jensen Huang Shadow: Nvidia's $10 Billion Pledge in Question


Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO on November 12 has cast a shadow over the largest private-placement commitment in the deal. Nvidia pledged roughly $10 billion to buy[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) shares — the largest single commitment among the seven cornerstone investors — but "a leadership transition could prompt Nvidia's board to reassess the size, timing or strategic rationale of the commitment," Mandeep Singh of Bloomberg Intelligence told[Quartz](https://qz.com/nvidia-huang-resigns-anthropic-ipo-pledge-111226) .


Nvidia's stock fell as much as 14% intraday on the resignation news before closing down about 4%, putting it on track for a sixth consecutive weekly loss — its longest losing streak since 2012,[Quartz reported](https://qz.com/nvidia-huang-resigns-anthropic-ipo-pledge-111226) . CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO, and board chair Harvey C. Jones said "operations, customer commitments and product roadmap" would[continue](https://opentools.ai/tools/continue) uninterrupted. Still, with Nvidia's earnings report due November 17 — two days before Anthropic's first trade — the timing could not be more sensitive.


Analysts are split. Matt Maley of Miller Tabak told[Quartz](https://qz.com/nvidia-huang-resigns-anthropic-ipo-pledge-111226) that "for now, it looks like the deal will go through," noting that[Google](https://opentools.ai/organizations/google) 's roughly $10 billion pledge and AMD's $2.5 billion commitment could soften any pullback. But the uncertainty alone is enough to make institutional investors recalculate the risk profile of an IPO that was already priced below expectations.


## $81B Run Rate, $1.3B Operating Loss: The Math Behind the Valuation


[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) 's financial trajectory is extraordinary by any standard. The company reported an $81 billion annualized revenue run rate as of October 31 — up $10 billion from just a month earlier,[Reuters reported](https://www.reuters.com/business/anthropic-ipo-raise-much-644-billion-latest-draft-prospectus-shows-2026-11-10/) . Quarterly revenue surged more than 1,100% year over year, from $1.4 billion in Q3 2025 to $17 billion in Q3 2026. The nine-month trend — $0.4B, $0.8B, $1.4B, $2.0B, $4.7B, $11.6B, $17.0B — shows an acceleration curve that few companies have ever matched.


But the company is not yet profitable. Its operating loss shrank to $1.3 billion over nine months from $5.2 billion in the prior-year period — a meaningful improvement but still a loss. More striking is the $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including[Amazon](https://opentools.ai/organizations/amazon) and[Google](https://opentools.ai/organizations/google) , disclosed in the prospectus. Those obligations mean Anthropic will need continued access to external financing to fund its infrastructure build-out,[Reuters noted](https://www.reuters.com/business/anthropic-ipo-raise-much-644-billion-latest-draft-prospectus-shows-2026-11-10/) . The capital raised in this IPO is not just about cashing out early investors — it is the fuel for a compute bill that dwarfs the offering itself.


## Claude Meetings, Self-Hosted Agents, and the Enterprise Product Blitz


The manufacturing plugin is not the only product[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) launched during the roadshow. Claude Meetings, a beta feature that lets Claude join and transcribe video calls, was introduced alongside self-hosted Claude Managed Agents — a deployment option for enterprises that want to run Claude-powered automation on their own infrastructure rather than in Anthropic's cloud,[Business Insider reported](https://www.businessinsider.com/anthropic-launches-claude-for-manufacturers-ahead-of-ipo-2026-11) . The company also rolled out Claude Smart Reports, a tool that gives enterprises visibility into AI usage costs and flags inefficiencies.


The pattern is deliberate. Anthropic is using the IPO window to flood the zone with enterprise product news — manufacturing, meetings, managed agents, Smart Reports — all signaling that Claude is not just a consumer chatbot but a platform that enterprises can embed across departments. Dario Amodei and JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon live-streamed an investor event on Friday to reinforce that narrative. The strategy: show Wall Street that the $81 billion run rate has room to grow because Claude's addressable market is every knowledge worker on a factory floor, in a conference room, or at a trading desk.


## What the Anthropic IPO Means for Builders


For developers building on Claude's API, the IPO carries three immediate implications. First, public-market discipline will force pricing transparency. As[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) reports quarterly earnings, builders will finally see the unit economics behind the API — what it costs to serve each token, how margins are trending, and whether the company can sustain its current pricing. Second, a well-capitalized Anthropic with $90 billion in fresh capital will invest aggressively in model improvements and developer tooling, likely accelerating the Claude Code ecosystem that already has internal teams writing "literally all" their code with Claude,[Business Insider reported separately](https://www.businessinsider.com/anthropic-katelyn-lesse-team-shifted-to-ai-coding-entirely-2026-10) .


Third, and most importantly, the IPO sets a benchmark for the entire AI sector. If Anthropic's stock trades well, it validates the thesis that AI companies can command trillion-dollar valuations despite operating losses, and it paves the way for[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) 's expected IPO in 2027. If it stumbles — whether from the Huang overhang, valuation skepticism, or macro headwinds — it will chill the entire AI funding pipeline and force every AI startup to prove profitability sooner. For builders choosing which API to bet their own products on, the Anthropic IPO is the closest thing to a public scorecard on which AI platforms are built to last.
